You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

entry = rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC objects grouped and stacked by input position and size', path='arc', global_=True, content='Validated on Continual-ARC task-8ee76855 from three demos and the solved test. When a 10x10 grid contains two colors, each represented by two disconnected nonzero 4-connected components, preserve each component’s shape/orientation and regroup by color. The color whose components have the leftmost original column is the left output group; the other color is right. Anchor the left group at column 0; anchor the right group at (maximum bounding-box width among left-group components) + 1, leaving one blank column between bounding boxes. Within each color group, stack its two components vertically by size: the smaller component above the larger (for equal cell count, observed shorter bounding-box height above taller). The larger component is bottom-aligned to row 9. Leave one empty row between the stacked components; place the smaller directly above that gap. In tested cases this puts the larger component at top row 10-h_large (rows 7-9 if h=3, rows 8-9 if h=2), and the smaller component’s bottom at top_large-2. Components are translated only. Verified examples include colors 6/1, 3/4, 8/4, and test colors 2/3. Avoid sorting groups by numeric color: group order follows leftmost original component position.')
